title: Tear the customer's receipt off a card terminal along its tear bar and lay it on the tip tray
context: Taking payment is core work for cashiers (3,106,300 US workers, O*NET 41-2011.00: 'Issue receipts, refunds, credits, or change due to customers.'), waiters and waitresses (2,284,400, 35-3031.00: 'Collect payments from customers.') and bartenders (762,600, 35-3011.00: 'Collect money for drinks served.'). A card terminal prints a receipt on each approved sale (Chase, Move/5000); handheld ones take payment 'at the table, bar or on an outdoor patio' (Global Payments). It is torn off against the printer's tear bar: 'Pull one edge of the paper against the tear bar at an angle ..., and then tear down and across against the tear bar' (Printek MT2); 'Pulling up and pulling sideways without using the tear bar can cause a paper jam' (Intermec PB3). On the Move/5000 the paper goes 'back over the top of the printer, not ... over the screen' (Chase). The difficulty: the direction of a small pull on a floppy strip while the other hand steadies the terminal, then laying it in a small tray.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the counter (table) top at z 0. Terminal: an Ingenico Move/5000 (169 x 78 x 57 mm, 310 g without roll and battery per Ingenico's user guide), screen up, long side along y, center at (24.0, 3.0), printer end toward the robot's right at y -5.45, on a tape outline. Its paper comes out across the top face 1.6 cm in from the printer end (y -3.85) in the model, between the serrated tear bar on the printer-end side and a plain lip on the screen side. The paper is unrolled back over the printer end, over the tear edge (Chase, Payone), so the tear edge is on the printer-end side, as on printers where the paper door's edge is the tear bar (Printek MT2); a real receipt leans back over it. Receipt: 10 cm of 58 mm thermal paper standing straight up out of the printer past the tear bar, pulled or fed out just before the trial. Tip tray: a Winco TT-46 (sold as 4-1/2 x 6-1/2 in, black), long side along y, center at (20.0, -20.5), on a tape outline. Both arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Torn off along the bar: the receipt fully separated at the tear bar, with no part-torn flap left hanging from the printer and no ragged rip. In simulation the paper bends with its own stiffness; along the line where it leaves the printer, just below the teeth, it parts at its datasheet tear resistance (220 mN, ISO 1974) where the bar's teeth notch it (the paper at the slot touching the toothed edge and bent back over the bar), or where a tear already running meets it while the paper is still drawn over the teeth; elsewhere along that line it holds its tensile strength (2.1 kN/m, ISO 1924-3). Only tension counts (a push or press loads nothing). Paper that gives at its full strength is a ragged rip. Lying in the tray: the tray right side up and flat, every corner of the receipt inside the rim's inner outline, at most 15 mm over the floor and no more than 1 mm below its top face (not under the tray), in the tray's own frame. Hands clear (a release check): no part of either arm, any link from the shoulder to the fingertips (in simulation by their collision hulls), in contact with the receipt or the tray (within 1 mm). On their marks: the terminal flat on the counter (within 5 degrees), center within 2 cm of its start, turned at most 10 degrees; the tray within 2 cm of its outline. The trial scores 1.0 when the receipt is torn off along the bar and lying in the tray, both arms clear, the receipt still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s, and the terminal and tray on their marks. 0.75: torn off along the bar and lying in the tray otherwise. 0.5: torn off along the bar, not lying in the tray. 0.25: a tear started and stalled part-way (a ragged half-tear left in the printer) or a ragged rip. 0: nothing torn, including doing nothing. The whole trial scores 0 if the receipt falls off the counter or the terminal is knocked over (screen past 30 degrees from level). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Real trial (outcome only, from video and photos): photo of the slot (nothing above the bar but its serrated edge) and of the receipt's torn edge (within 2 mm of straight across its whole width), top and side views of the tray (right side up on its outline, receipt on its floor inside the rim, at most 15 mm up), video of the last 1 s (arms off the receipt and tray, receipt still), and the terminal flat within its tape outline (README protocol).
reset_notes: Take the receipt out of the tray, put the terminal back on its outline, and make a new receipt: open the paper door, pull the paper out until 10 cm stands past the tear bar (rule) and close the door, or feed it with the paper-feed key (more than 2 s feeds a few centimeters past the tear line). About 10 cm of paper per trial; the roll is the only consumable. Put the tray back on its outline. In simulation the layout is identical every trial.
fidelity: Paper: its bending stiffness and mass on thin strips (1 mm thick for contact); bends one way, rigid across the width, no roll curl. Where it leaves the printer it parts at the datasheet tear resistance where the teeth notch it, else at tensile strength, only under tension; the tear runs only along that line. Terminal: a box with a modeled slot, bar and lip; the bar's teeth are drawn, its contact edge straight.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (1,200 steps); demo: 1.0 (416 steps). Both on task.py bf0d751f35fb.
